title: Fiber cardinality identity
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic protocol on pairs of subsets of an $n$-element coordinate set, and let $z$ be an achievable value of the summary consisting of the protocol transcript, the special coordinate, Alice’s bits strictly before it, and Bob’s bits strictly after it. For any pair of bits $b=(b_1,b_2)$, the number of samples in the fiber $Z=z$ with Alice’s special bit equal to $b_1$, multiplied by the number with Bob’s special bit equal to $b_2$, equals the number in that fiber whose pair of special bits is $b$, multiplied by the size of the fiber.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic protocol on pairs of subsets of an $n$-element coordinate set
$b$ is a pair of Boolean values
replaced:
Fix a positive integer $n$, a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for disjointness
inputs of length $n$, an achievable value $z$ of the associated $Z$-variable, and a pair
of bits $b=(b_1,b_2)$. Let $F$ be the fiber consisting of those hard-distribution
samples $\omega$ whose $Z$-variable equals $z$, and for such a sample write
$x_T(\omega)$ for Alice's bit at the special coordinate and $y_T(\omega)$ for Bob's bit
at the special coordinate. Then
\[
\abs{\{\omega\in F : x_T(\omega)=b_1\}}\cdot\abs{\{\omega\in F : y_T(\omega)=b_2\}}
=\abs{\{\omega\in F : (x_T(\omega),y_T(\omega))=b\}}\cdot\abs{F}.
\]
